letters.notes: jiim -- the ONLY new letter today, taught alone on purpose: 'jiim, Haa, and khaa, they look like each other. I don't want to introduce them all in one session' (3898-3903); 'practice jiim... because I'm going to teach you also the Haa and the khaa' Thursday (4738-4746). Shape (3940-3976): 'It's like a triangle and I go down, then there is a dot here. If I'm writing on the line, the triangle goes above the line, I go under the line, and make sure this is a little bit curvy.' A sharp corner 'is not wrong. I don't like it'. Print/book font has a GAP instead of a closed triangle -- 'Choose whatever is easy for you' (3978-4003). 'jiim connects both sides, therefore we have four shapes' (4005-4018). MEDIAL in her handwriting is a ZIGZAG: 'you go left, right, left'; start a little above the line to leave room (4033-4063); she also showed lifting the pen after the connector (4077-4093). The book does not teach the zigzag: 'if you don't like it, don't do it' (4211-4220). FINAL: 'zigzag, then you go under' the line (4111-4145). A letter before jiim (baa, taa) ends up STACKED on top of it -- fine; if you don't stack, keep the connector 'dash size' because a long one 'might be perceived as a siin, coming in the future' (4145-4159, 4583-4638). Sound: the book lists j (as in jack), zh (Levant, as in French bonjour) and hard g (Cairo); she said it 'has the sound of j... or zh' (4005-4014, partly unclear). Practice words at the board: جاب jaab, تُجيب tujiib, بيج beige.
